terms.meaning: The single source file that defines the slides, their wording, citations and facts.
A record of where each claim came from, such as its citations and supporting facts.
Hidden text stored with each slide in the deck, used here to hold a machine-readable record.
A clickable link in a slide, either to a web address or to another slide.
A compressed bundle of files. A PowerPoint deck is one, and the script reads it directly.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Reading the deck, text and speaker notes
sections.what: Opens the deck and compares each slide's visible text with the model. For each slide it also reads the hidden notes and compares the slide id, citations, original wording and each supporting fact. It then checks every hyperlink to confirm it is a web link or points to a real slide.
sections.why: The docstring says the check proves that text, sources and links match the model. The speaker notes carry the machine-readable record that makes this comparison possible.
sections.watch_out: The notes are parsed by taking everything between the first opening brace and the last closing brace, so any extra braces in the notes make the check report invalid provenance.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Writing the report and exit code
sections.what: Checks that every fact record in the model was seen in the notes. Writes a report with pass or fail, the counts of pages, fact records and links checked, the list of checks, and the list of items not covered. Prints the report and sets the exit code to failure when any issue was found.
sections.why: The notCovered list tells the reader what still needs a human eye, such as layout and clickable target placement.
sections.watch_out: A pass means only the listed checks passed. The notCovered items, such as visual layout and browser parity, still need a separate check.

summary: Checks a generated slide deck against its source model for text, hidden provenance notes, citations, supporting facts and links. It never claims a visual check.
purpose: Confirms that the deck's words and records match the canonical model, and writes a pass or fail report.
why: The docstring says the check covers content, provenance and links only. The report's notCovered list states the visual items it does not check.
how: Takes three arguments: the model file, the deck file and the report path. Opens the deck as a zip archive and, for each slide, checks that the title, subtitle, bullets and footnotes appear in the slide text. It reads each slide's hidden notes, comparing the slide id, citations, original wording and supporting facts with the model. It then checks each hyperlink: external links must be web links, and internal links must point to a real slide. It writes the report, prints it and exits with failure if any issue was found.
inputs: The canonical model JSON file, the PowerPoint deck, and the output report path.
outputs: A JSON report file written to the given path, the same report printed to the console, and an exit code of zero for pass or one for fail.
risks: The notes check takes everything between the first opening brace and the last closing brace, so any other brace in the notes breaks the parse. Only the first slide-count mismatch is reported, and later slides are checked against whatever pages exist. The report folder must already exist.
debug: Read the issues list in the report, which names the slide and the kind of problem. If a slide reports invalid provenance, check the notes text for stray braces. If a link is flagged unsafe, check its target. If the count of fact records is short, check the portable notes.
